Content:
20:05 Mark this is called photobleaching. Floaters aren’t a new phenomenon and it’s basically our eye trying to heal what we just hurt in ourselves with (the light sensitive cells are unable to process as much light as before which makes “blind spots”).

They can take on shapes that might appear like symbols, especially if it was something that had lettering on it—such as a McDonalds sign that might be a little too bright for you to process right (so you might see a giant floating ‘M’ in your vision)—but most people are familiar with blobs.

Content:
Hey, the letters in light! I get something very similar, that really confused me for a while: I have an alarm on my phone, that to turn it off has a big button that says "Dismiss" that you push to turn it off. Whenever I've just awoken and look at the button right away, the letters are always different and sometimes changing, and sometimes symbols instead.

I thought for a little bit that it was some weird feature that would display "Dismiss" in all different languages or something. Had to test it while I was awake to assure myself that it never *actually* changes from saying "Dismiss." Have never heard anyone experiencing anything similar. Can very reliably repeat it if I look at my phone immediately on waking, though sometimes the effect lasts longer than others before solidifying back into a normal "Dismiss."

Edit: Have also tested words on a page in a book, it weirded up a *little* bit but not nearly as much. The "illuminated" aspect of the phone seems to help thoroughly confuse my brain on bootup, idk.
